text:
infra-bot: ALERT: p99 streaming decode latency > 1200ms in us-west-2 for the streaming endpoint (service: inference-stream). Detected at 2024-10-12T02:07:48Z. Auto-escalation to oncall.

jess: seeing it on dashboards, p95 also creeping up (~420ms). Tons of tail spikes after the 02:00 kernel rollout.

michael: confirm — traces show long waits inside kernel decode path, increased page fault counts per GPU. linking traces: https://internal.traces/replay/abcd1234

jess: @tasha @ryan can you join? customer-impact looks like degraded streaming for some top-tier customers (slow token streaming, extra latency on initial decode).

tasha: joining. I pulled a flamegraph, looks like the new compilepath option `-Oflash-kernel` introduced in the build is hot in the stack.

ryan: fyi we pushed TRT/FlashAttention-optimized kernels in last deploy window to reduce cost. Could be regressed mapping for certain seq lengths.

sam: customer-success-bot reports two active tickets citing timeouts during streaming. CC: @customer-success-bot for any live customer notes.

customer-success-bot: Customers A and B flagged slow streaming; both using long-history chat (avg seq 1024). No full timeouts yet, but user-visible lag.

michael: logs from the nodes show repeated mmap/evict cycles and `CUDA_ERROR_LAUNCH_TIMEOUT`-style symptoms on 4/32 hosts. Suspect paging/compilepath eviction interaction.

jess: immediate ask: can we fallback routes to a known-safe kernel variant? Is there a fast rollback?

tasha: we have a previous kernel tag `kernel-2.1.6-stable` in the artifact registry. We can trigger a canary rollback for the streaming fleet.

ryan: before rollback, quick mitigation: enable runtime fallback to `decode-safe` path via config flag on router: `DECODE_RUNTIME_FALLBACK=true`. That bypasses the new fast kernel and keeps older nv kernels. Applying to 20% first.

jess: do it. command?

tasha: run:
```
kubectl -n inference set env deployment/inference-router DECODE_RUNTIME_FALLBACK=true --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
kubectl -n streaming rollout restart deployment/inference-router -l rollout=canary
```

ryan: applying to canary now. watching p99.

deploy-bot: deploy request accepted. rollout started for label rollout=canary.

michael: while that's rolling, we should gather kernel build diffs. The compile flags changed: `-fno-stack-protector` removed, `-Oflash-attn` added. Might be aggressive inlining changing memory access patterns.

jess: noted. @michael can you paste the `dmesg` snippet from an affected host?

michael: snippet:
```
[Oct12 02:03:12] gpu0: mmap evict triggered, seq=1024, active pages=1.2M
[Oct12 02:03:13] kernel: page fault, cs=0x1 dev=nvme0n1
[Oct12 02:03:14] gpu0: kernel compilepath load time 138ms (expected 12ms)
```

tasha: that compilepath load time jump is the smoking gun. If the runtime is compiling kernels lazily for certain sequence shapes we get stalls.

ryan: can we pre-warm the kernel cache for the common seq lengths? Maybe as a short term reduce tail.

jess: good idea. How fast to pre-warm?

tasha: I can push a pre-warm job to load kernels for seq=128,256,512,1024 across nodes. It will bump CPU/IO briefly but should cut later loads. Command:
```
python infra/tools/prewarm_kernels.py --seq 128,256,512,1024 --nodes-tag streaming-usw2
```

michael: prewarm running, starting to see some p99 improvement on canary hosts (down from 1200ms -> ~650ms).

jess: good. keep canary for 10 minutes and monitor. If stable, we roll to 50%, then full. Meanwhile flag for rollback if regressions persist.

sam: logging customer notifications: telling affected accounts we have identifying the cause and mitigation steps, will update within 30m.

customer-success-bot: Notified customers A,B with a brief status update.

ryan: telemetry: paging rate has dropped ~45% on canary after fallback + prewarm. Streaming token rates steady.

michael: one more datapoint — models instantiated with longer KV caches tend to hit this harder. Likely interplay with KV memory eviction and the new kernel cache allocation scheme.

tasha: next steps: create a hotfix kernel build that disables `-Oflash-attn` in compile flags and keeps other improvements. Then run a staged rollout.

jess: can we ship that hotfix within the hour?

tasha: yes, building now. ETA 28m to artifact, 5m to canary deploy.

deploy-bot: build pipeline started for `kernel-hotfix-176880`. CI tests running.

michael: meanwhile, ops checklist — escalate to SRE lead if p99 > 1s after full rollout plan. Also gather heap snapshots from affected GPUs.

jess: noted. @ryan prepare an incident summary for postmortem: timeline, kernel diff, compile flags, which models impacted, mitigation steps. We'll capture customer impact numbers (requests affected, error/latency delta).

ryan: copying commands for snapshots:
```
ssh gpu-node-12
sudo nvprof --kernels "decode*" --output nvprof-node12.log
sudo dd if=/proc/pagemap of=/tmp/pagemap-node12 bs=4096 count=262144
```

tasha: hotfix build finished, pushing to artifact registry, canary rollout initiated.

deploy-bot: canary rollout for kernel-hotfix-176880 applied to 12 pods.

michael: canary p99 down to ~320ms, p95 180ms. This is promising.

jess: good work. schedule: keep canary for 15m, then 50% for 10m, then 100% if no regressions. Update incident status in 30m.

sam: customer update drafted, will send after 15m if metrics hold.

customer-success-bot: Customers A and B acknowledged, appreciate prompt response.

jess: handoff plan — I'm on until 03:30Z. @tasha you'll remain on the thread for the rollback/hotfix verification. If anything worsens during my handoff, escalate to SRE lead @michael.

tasha: ack. leaving notes in incident doc with kernel diffs and prewarm commands.

michael: I'll start collecting artifacts for the postmortem now.

infra-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: p99 improved from 1200ms -> 320ms after kernel-hotfix rollout. Canary -> 100% planned. No service-level breaches currently open.

jess: closing loop — will update timeline in incidents/1768802468 doc. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

ryan: quick suggestion for follow-up: add prewarm to deployment pipeline when a kernel compilepath change lands, and add a canary traffic generator for long-seq workloads.

jess: agreed — add to postmortem action items.

customer-success-bot: Final customer note queued for send after confirmation of full rollout.

jess: thread will remain open for 2h for monitoring. If anything surfaces ping oncall.
